graph.title: LEGO Architecture 21033 Chicago
notes: The manual's pictures are small and several steps do not show which stud a piece lands on. Part identities and counts were reconciled against the inventory page (every element ID and quantity matches), but the exact stacking neighbour for many plates is my best interpretation.

Port usage fix: a stud port can only be used once, and most catalogue plates expose only one 'stud.1'/'anti-stud.1' port (379526 has no anti-stud at all). Named ports are therefore used only on one-to-one chains (the b1-b6 base start, the Wrigley stack, the Willis narrow tower, the Hancock yellow column and top). Every one-to-many connection (host plates carrying several parts, floor layers, facade ridged plates, side attachments, clips, rods in sockets) uses null ports. Incompatible port pairs (stud/pin-hole, pin-hole/bar, clip/clip, stud/stud) were also removed that way.
Everything is modelled as `joined`. No electrical edges apply.

Willis Tower: lower module (steps 50-58), 5 lower layers (59), 4 upper layers (61-63), side tiers (66-72), cross-plate crown (73-74), narrow tower (75-77). Each layer is a 3x3 plate (6174917) plus four trans-smoke 1x2 plates (6001197), matching inventory counts (13x 6174917, 58x 6001197, 22x 6030982).

Big Red: 4 floor-core assemblies plus red bracket pairs (36-45), 2 roof plate assemblies (46) and a roof tile (47). Floors 1 and 3 have four grille plates per bracket, floors 2 and 4 a tile plus two grille plates (from the parts boxes).
Pavement pieces (light-grey corner plates, jumpers, round plates, tiles, long plates) are repeated pieces attached to the dark base plates; their exact positions are approximate.

Hancock Center: yellow core column (95), clip frame (96-98, two arms) and two ridged-plate facades (100-110) in the manual's order. The arms clip onto the top plate and the tan clip plates b28/b30 in the base. The 6176433 quarter-round tiles at page 98 are attached to the round plate under the Wrigley Building (placement unclear). The single-use-port warnings on host plates were not real defects of the manual, only of my earlier port naming.

New part types were added for 19 element IDs missing from the catalogue (e.g. 6001197, 6030982, 6097283, 6118830, 6135607, 6071229, 4211511, 6177165). Names and port lists are inferred from the pictures.

graph_initial.title: LEGO Architecture 21033 Chicago
notes: The manual's pictures are small and several steps do not show which stud a piece lands on. Part identities and counts were reconciled against the inventory page (every element ID and quantity matches), but the exact stacking neighbour for many plates is my best interpretation.
Everything is modelled as `joined` (stud/anti-stud etc.). No electrical edges apply.
Element colours are given as colour props. Parts listed in the catalogue as 'black' are shown dark grey in the manual and are kept as black.

Willis Tower: the lower module (steps 50-58) and 5 lower layers (step 59), 4 upper layers (61-63), side tiers (66-72), cross-plate crown (73-74), narrow tower (75-77). Each layer is a 3x3 plate (6174917) plus four trans-smoke 1x2 plates (6001197), which is the best reading of the inventory counts (13x 6174917, 58x 6001197, 22x 6030982).

Big Red: 4 floor-core assemblies plus red bracket pairs (steps 36-45), 2 roof plate assemblies (46) and a roof tile (47). Each floor stacks on the previous floor's top green plate. Floors 1 and 3 have four grille plates per bracket, floors 2 and 4 have a tile plus two grille plates (from the parts boxes).

The 12 light-grey corner plates, 8 jumper plates, round plates, tiles and long plates of the pavement are repeated pieces all attached to the dark base plates (b6 or b15). Their individual positions on the base are approximate.

Hancock Center: the yellow core column (step 95), the clip-frame (96-98 x2 arms) and the two ridged-plate facades (100-110 x2) are joined in the manual's order. The arms clip onto the top plate and the tan clip plates b28/b30 in the base. Facade-to-core attachments are approximated. The 6176433 quarter-round tiles shown at page 98 are attached to the round plate under the Wrigley Building (placement unclear).
Side-attached parts (white window plates and slopes on the Wrigley Building, grille plates on the red brackets) use null ports because the catalogue has no named side-stud ports for them.

New part types were added for 19 element IDs missing from the catalogue (e.g. 6001197, 6030982, 6097283, 6118830, 6135607, 6071229, 4211511, 6177165). Names and port lists are inferred from the pictures.
